harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed inventory-worker as a hardened systemd service on node1: dedicated unprivileged user/group, /var/lib/inventory data dir, a simple long-running tick loop, and a unit with NoNewPrivileges=yes plus ProtectSystem=strict/ReadWritePaths confinement to /var/lib/inventory (plus other standard sandboxing directives). Falsification test proved writes outside the allowed path fail (read-only) while writes inside succeed. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured boot_id/service baseline, rebooted node1, confirmed boot_id changed, and verified the service came back enabled/active with persisted state.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS/privileges (RHEL 10, root, systemd 257)
Created system user/group inventory-worker (no login shell, no home)
Created /var/lib/inventory owned by inventory-worker, mode 750
Wrote /usr/local/bin/inventory-worker.sh: infinite loop appending to inventory.log and persisting a counter, sleep 10 between ticks

Wrote /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service with User/Group=inventory-worker, NoNewPrivileges=yes, ProtectSystem=strict, ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory, StateDirectory=inventory, plus ProtectHome/PrivateTmp/PrivateDevices/CapabilityBoundingSet= and other lockdown directives
Ran systemd-analyze verify to confirm unit correctness
systemctl daemon-reload; enable --now inventory-worker.service; confirmed active/running via status
Verified /var/lib/inventory contains count and inventory.log owned by inventory-worker, and systemctl show confirms NoNewPrivileges/ReadWritePaths/ProtectSystem/User/CapabilityBoundingSet
Ran a systemd-run transient unit with the same sandbox properties to falsify: write to /etc failed (read-only filesystem), write to /var/lib/inventory succeeded
Cleaned up test artifact and transient unit
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, uptime, systemctl is-enabled/is-active, counter value
Scheduled systemctl reboot via backgrounded nohup so the exec acknowledgement returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again; confirmed boot_id changed (636556ce... -> c8000397...)
Verified post-restart: service enabled and active with a fresh invocation ID, and counter/log continued incrementing from persisted state

evidence.requirement: inventory-worker deployed as a managed (systemd) service, long-running
evidence.summary: Worker script and systemd unit created, unit verified clean, service started and shown active/running with worker+sleep processes in its cgroup

Directory created and owned by service user; systemctl show confirms ProtectSystem=strict and ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory; only expected files (count, inventory.log) present and owned by inventory-worker
Unit defines NoNewPrivileges=yes and CapabilityBoundingSet=; systemctl show confirms both properties are set on the running unit
Transient unit with identical sandbox properties: write to /etc/should-fail failed with 'Read-only file system' (exit 1) while write to /var/lib/inventory/should-succeed succeeded (exit 0)

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id=636556ce-a308-49cc-b873-62cedb1c077d, service enabled+active, counter=2 prior to reboot

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: acknowledgement returns before disconnection
evidence.summary: Backgrounded 'sleep 2; systemctl reboot' via nohup/disown so the exec call returned REBOOT_SCHEDULED immediately, before the node disconnected

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: changed boot identity proves an actual restart occurred
evidence.summary: Polling showed connection timeout then reset while node was down/rebooting; once reachable again, boot_id read as c8000397-abec-446d-9a56-d66a87877c3b, differing from the pre-restart value

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: post-restart recovery of required service and data
evidence.summary: After reboot, inventory-worker.service is enabled and active with a new invocation ID; persisted counter/log continued from prior value (3->4->5) and kept ticking, proving both the service and its confined data survived and resumed
